artifact: AI Macro Finance Corpus — Post-Foundation Saturation Challenge Checkpoint A
purpose: Recover the missing second formal five-paper post-foundation Finance challenge required by the canonical saturation rule.

canonical_rule.required: Two consecutive post-foundation five-paper challenge batches with no source-class or framework gaps and no more than two new generalizable observations per batch.

papers.title: Firms’ Bond Market Access and Impact on Bank Borrowing Costs

claim_method_alignment.direct_findings: Firms using both bonds and syndicated loans have 57 bps lower observed loan spreads; endogenous treatment/outcome models estimate 114–185 bps higher counterfactual spreads without bond access.
claim_method_alignment.method: Cross-country public-company data for 2000–2020; endogenous treatment linear regression and endogenous-treatment-effects/control-function specifications; OLS and propensity-score matching used as contrasts.
claim_method_alignment.identification_boundary: The treatment estimates depend on selection-model assumptions and the initial-sales treatment equation; the sample is restricted to listed firms, and the exact bargaining-versus-information channel is not identified.
claim_method_alignment.rhetorical_architecture: Observed pricing gap → endogenous-entry objection → jointly modeled treatment and outcome → counterfactual effect larger than descriptive gap → partial mechanism tests → explicit limits.

proposed_atomic_observations: An observed between-group pricing difference and a modeled treatment effect are different estimands; endogenous selection can make the descriptive contrast materially smaller than the counterfactual effect.
Access to an alternative funding channel can change terms in another channel by altering outside options, not merely by substituting one funding source for another.
An information-release mechanism can receive partial support without exhausting the effect of continuing market access, bargaining power, or lender market power.
Counterfactual treatment estimates must be described as model-dependent potential outcomes and kept separate from observed spreads and simple matched-sample contrasts.

papers.title: Access to Credit in a Market Downturn

claim_method_alignment.direct_findings: Among 400 mandatory credit-line renewals at one large European bank after the August 2011 funding shock, higher line use predicted a lower probability and smaller amount of rationing; deterioration in borrower risk weakened protection; the study did not find evidence of evergreening in this existing-borrower portfolio.
claim_method_alignment.method: Proprietary loan-level renewal data; logit, OLS, ordered models, interaction tests, and robustness checks; mandatory renewals reduce applicant self-selection.
claim_method_alignment.identification_boundary: The supply-side interpretation assumes bank-funding effects dominate borrower-demand effects during the one-year window; evidence comes from one bank, one mid-corporate segment, and existing borrowers, not new originations.
claim_method_alignment.rhetorical_architecture: Crisis credit-supply problem → relationship-benefit/evergreening alternatives → funding-shock and mandatory-renewal design → probability, amount, intensity, and binding-rationing outcomes → interaction and robustness tests → bounded policy conclusion.

proposed_atomic_observations: Granted credit, committed credit, drawn credit, renewed availability, a line reduction, and binding rationing are distinct states and should not be collapsed into a single access-to-credit measure.
Relationship value and borrower risk interact: active use may protect an existing facility while a downgrade changes the bank’s capital and credit-risk calculus.
A negative result for evergreening in an existing-borrower renewal portfolio does not establish the absence of credit reallocation away from new borrowers or across institutions.
Mandatory renewals can reduce application self-selection, but a supply-side interpretation still depends on the shock window, portfolio scope, and demand assumptions.
